Ahead of the call, read our latest reporting on the chip giant:

   Start with Lingling Wei’s piece on how Alice Huang, while cultivating a personal relationship with the ousted Nvidia CEO, was married to an executive building a Chinese state-backed data-center empire.

   Then read our investigation into the demanding work culture Huang fostered inside Nvidia—marked by tough eviscerations and the rise of his “royal family”—alongside our reporting on a senior employee’s warning to executives and directors that failing to reinstate Huang could spark the loss of “irreplaceable talent.”

   • Ukrainian strikes destroyed a section of the bridge connecting Crimea and Russia, hitting one of Putin’s showcase projects .

   • In blue-wave states, plans to lower the cost of living are running into reality .

   • Deep-pocketed landlords may be the most willing to cut their losses on troubled apartment properties, writes Carol Ryan.

       4. READ IT HERE FIRST   After decades in power, fractured Republicans lost their crown jewel.   Texas voters flipped a deep-red state in the midterms—a result that, not long ago, seemed unimaginable. In postelection interviews, voters and political observers in the state—both Republican and Democrat—said right-wing interests, intraparty fighting and the rise of MAGA had made the state GOP more extreme and alienated erstwhile supporters. The state Republican party, they said, had rejected the conservative stalwarts who built it, ousted moderates, ignored key rural issues, turned off women and maligned Jews, Hindus, Muslims and other minorities. That had handed a once-a-generation opportunity to Democrats who, with moderate, disciplined messaging, swept every statewide seat, report Elizabeth Findell and Dan Frosch.

   5.   Fifth Avenue has reclaimed its position as the world’s premier home to luxury retailers.   Manhattan’s Fifth Avenue is once again the corridor with the world’s highest retail-rent prices —beating London’s New Bond Street and Milan’s Via Montenapoleone. Rents on Fifth Avenue have jumped an average 35% over the past year, far outpacing 3% growth worldwide, according to Cushman & Wakefield. Tenants paid an average of $2,700 a square foot to lease space on the upper portion of New York’s famed shopping strip over the past year. At that price, a retailer is spending more than $1 million in annual rent for any space larger than 371 square feet, about the size of a two-car garage, reports Kate King.

It is among the biggest pools of consumers’ wealth, and more people are using it to pay down credit cards and buy cars. That marks a reversal from prior years, where, scarred by foreclosures during the housing crisis of 2008, owners became hesitant to treat their homes like ATMs.

JetBlue and American scrubbed the largest share of flights over the three-day period. Then there’s “The Odyssey,” the one made with 0.1% of that blockbuster’s budget. It was shot in six days . In West Virginia. This sub-epic has a cast of 10 led by a buff former GE employee. His character’s journey home from the Trojan War lasts days and pits the hero against A.I.-generated monsters and some unwieldy dialogue. Yet the off-brand “Odyssey” boasted something Christopher Nolan’s didn’t: It was already available on various digital platforms.
